subject: project:gdl
value: R67 produced actionable reconstruction repairs and positive compiler-capability controls, not a proof that WebFrank is necessary or unnecessary for every function. The strongest demonstrated project-wide obstacle is incomplete source/data ownership and cross-TU integration, which the normal mixed-source/extracted matching DOL can conceal. Priority is a faithful all-configured-source link and correct whole-TU data/interface context, followed by controlled raw compiler/source-shape closure. Do not interpret finite negative flag matrices, a high fuzzy score, a common pool base, or an instruction-only exact diagnostic as historical source/compiler proof. The project remains incomplete: no new TU flip in this audit, no new WebFrank rules, no compiler RE or new patch.
